justification: Documentation only, plus one comment block in frontend-nextjs/app/api/dcp/coverage/route.ts. No executable statement changed anywhere: the route's SQL, predicates and response shape are byte-identical, and the diff there is entirely inside a comment. No database read or write, no migration, no served output, no dependency change. Exactly one file in the diff is substantive by the gate's own definition, which is within the minor-tier floor of three. Minor is claimed because the change cannot alter behaviour, not because it is small.

break_it.scenario: The corrected numbers themselves go stale, and this commit becomes the next false premise it was written to prevent. CLAUDE.md now states 116 base tables, 55,696 provisions, 433 precincts and 1,071 controls; every one of those moves whenever data is loaded.
break_it.how: Each figure is published beside the exact query that produces it, in a table whose stated contract is 're-run it rather than quoting this file'. A reader who follows the instruction gets today's number, not the committed one. This converts the claim from an assertion into an instruction, which is the only form that survives drift. The measurement date is stamped on the table.
break_it.what_happens: CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded into every session, so a stale figure there is read as fact by every future prompt before any measurement happens. That is precisely how '47,818 provisions' and 'former_council' survived for months and reached a session brief as a premise.

break_it.scenario: The production flag flips — DCP is switched off, or the LGA list is edited in Vercel — and docs/CONFIGURATION.md is wrong again in exactly the way this commit fixes. Nothing in CI reads Vercel environment variables, so no gate can notice.
break_it.how: The doc no longer asserts the value as a fact to be trusted; it records the verification procedure (fetch the deployed chunk, read whether the DCP_ENABLED guard survived constant-folding) and explicitly says the listed 29 slugs are not canonical and must be read from the bundle. A stale value therefore misleads only a reader who skips the stated check. Full mitigation would need a deployed-config probe in CI, which does not exist and is named as an open item rather than implied.
break_it.what_happens: A session reasoning about production reads 'DCP is off in prod', concludes the surface is dark, and either builds a redundant enablement path or reports to the founder that customers cannot see DCP data when 29 councils' worth is live.

break_it.scenario: A reader takes the unchanged doc_claims.py count of 145 findings as evidence the documents are now true, and stops checking.
break_it.how: The commit message states that the count is unchanged precisely because none of the five corrected errors is a path, version or dependency claim, so the checker structurally could not have caught any of them. doc_claims.py's own module docstring makes the same point ('do not read a green run as the docs are true'). The number is reported as a non-signal, not as a pass.
break_it.what_happens: The documents keep drifting while a green-looking gate implies they do not, which is the exact 'check that cannot fail' failure this project has already hit four times (0% drift, 13/16 confirmations, CI red three days, silently skipped tests).

break_it.scenario: The route.ts comment edit accidentally changes behaviour — e.g. a stray character breaks the template literal or comment terminator, so the SQL or the module fails to parse.
break_it.how: The change sits wholly inside an existing // comment run above the pool.query call and closes no block. Verified after editing: python -m pytest -q returns 3,970 passed / 2 skipped / 19 deselected (unchanged from the pre-edit baseline measured on the same worktree), scripts/validate_schema_contract.py returns PASSED with the same 10-entry baseline, and the pre-commit bracket/zone/fail-soft/fabricated-verdict lints all passed. TSC is skipped in a bare worktree by design and is enforced on deploy.
break_it.what_happens: The /api/dcp/coverage endpoint stops returning councils or 500s, so every surface asking 'which councils do you cover' renders empty — a silent coverage blackout rather than a visible error.

residual_risk: Three things this commit deliberately does NOT do. (1) It does not fix the Inner West exclusion in /api/dcp/coverage — the endpoint still returns 25 councils and still omits the three councils with the deepest DCP data. That is a behaviour change requiring a product ruling, so it is documented in the comment as a known gap rather than patched under a docs commit. (2) It does not touch .claude/DATA_QUALITY_TRACKER.md, which carries the largest share of doc_claims findings. Those references point at scripts/fixes/DQ*.py files that were real when the entries were written; the tracker is a historical audit record, and rewriting it to name files that exist today would falsify what was actually run, which is the same reasoning that preserved the 381 historic pvlib audit rows. (3) It does not un-stale tests/test_lga_coverage.py, the gate that would have prevented 13 councils with zero provisions entering NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLED_LGAS. That gate is now named in docs/CONFIGURATION.md as non-running, but switching it on would change what CI enforces and needs its own change. Additionally, doc_claims.py cannot check numeric or semantic claims at all, so the corrected counts in CLAUDE.md are protected by the published query and nothing else.

post_merge.db_reset: None. No migration, no schema change, no database write of any kind. This branch's only database contact was read-only SELECT and count(*) used to establish the corrected figures.
post_merge.secrets: None. No environment variable, key or credential is added, renamed or removed. The 29 LGA slugs recorded in docs/CONFIGURATION.md are public client-side values already inlined into the deployed JavaScript bundle and readable by any visitor, so documenting them discloses nothing.
post_merge.other_repo: None. No sibling repository, deployment target or external service is affected.
post_merge.manual_verify: After merge, confirm CLAUDE.md renders its new Database Quick Reference table correctly in a fresh session, since that file is auto-loaded into every session and a broken table would degrade every future prompt. Optionally re-run the two published queries to confirm the committed figures still hold: SELECT count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions (expect 55,696 at time of writing) and SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_type='BASE TABLE' (expect 116). A drift here is expected over time and is not a defect in this commit.
